claims.text: Lithographic patterning introduces interface defects or strain into as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films or nanoribbons.
Patterning-induced interface defects or strain alter magnetic anisotropy.
Patterning-induced interface defects or strain alter magnetic domain-wall dynamics.
Magnetic anisotropy and domain-wall dynamics govern the magnetocaloric response of the target low-dimensional alloy.
Magnetic anisotropy and domain-wall dynamics govern hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Introducing interface defects or strain through lithographic patterning enhances the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Introducing interface defects or strain through lithographic patterning reduces hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The proposed effects apply over 200–350 K.
The proposed effects apply at magnetic fields up to 1 T.
The proposed effects apply at cycling frequencies up to 10 Hz.
Heat-transfer rate limits affect the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.

contradictions.description: The initial state and baseline already include lithographically patterned nanoribbons, while lithographic patterning is also defined as the intervention that introduces defects or strain. The intervention and control are therefore not cleanly distinguished, and the baseline is simultaneously described as patterned and as lacking the patterning-induced features.
